reasons: Section 7.6 plainly imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer (USD 25,000/day for 'any delay'), with no cap on amount or duration and no materiality threshold — this fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs) and the fallback (single capped early-termination fee), and the unbounded daily accrual is squarely in walk-away territory, so the 'deviation' status is correct.
Direction is right: the rule flags only Customer-payable LDs, and here Customer is the payer; no Vendor-side service credits or offsetting LDs exist to make the clause acceptable.

Redline is actionable and reaches the playbook position: it removes Customer liability for liquidated damages/penalties and substitutes a neutral equitable schedule/Fee adjustment via change order conditioned on notice and mitigation — a defensible substitute rather than an unnecessary expansion of Customer obligations (any Fee change requires a change order).

The failed minimal-edit check (0.880 changed-character ratio) is expected here: deleting a Customer-payable LD obligation necessarily rewrites the whole clause, so the advisory heuristic does not indicate over-editing.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the three-month early-termination-fee fallback without lecturing.
